title: Incorporate incident learnings into PRD: deployment safeguards and acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: Update the product requirements document to capture concrete, testable safeguards derived from the recent cross-region KV cache incident. Translate postmortem action items into PRD requirements for deployment-time safety checks, deterministic fallback behavior, and acceptance criteria for automated rollouts. This PRD change will inform engineering tasks, release gating, and runbook updates.
background: A region-wide KV cache degradation in Jan caused elevated tail latency and partial model fallback loops that increased token costs and degraded user experience for several customers. Postmortem recommended: deterministic fallback paths, deployment-time policy checks, per-route circuit breakers, canary failure injection during CI, and SLO-triggered rollback automation. This ticket scopes how those items become formal PRD requirements with acceptance tests and release gates.
requirements: Requirement 1: Deterministic fallback policy: when primary model serving path exceeds configured latency threshold for >3s or KV cold-miss rate >10% for 2 consecutive minutes, route new requests to a predefined compatible model variant with bounded cost profile.

Requirement 2: Deployment safety checks: before rolling a model or runtime change, run automated preflight validations (capacity sanity, kv-health, kernel compatibility) and fail fast if any critical check fails.

Requirement 3: Per-route circuit breakers: define per-route SLOs and an automated circuit that returns structured degraded responses (error code + human-friendly fallback message) when error rate or latency breach persists for configured windows.

Requirement 4: Canary failure-injection tests: CI must run a controlled fault-injection matrix (KV cold miss, high token rate, worker OOM) against canaries and require green results before full rollout.

Requirement 5: Rollback & rollback acceptance: define automatic rollback triggers (SLO breach, rate of fallback > X, error budget burn) and require post-rollback validation before marking deploy as successful.

Requirement 6: Observability and runbook hooks: surface token-level cost delta, model routing delta, and failed-fallback counts in the Console with a dedicated incident dashboard template and runbook links.
Requirement 7: Customer-visible degradation contract: document response schema for degraded paths and ensure SDKs surface a consistent typed signal for downstream apps to handle gracefully.
scope_changes: Scope expanded from 'runtime fallback' to include deployment preflight validations and CI-level failure injection.
Remove: ad-hoc manual rollback procedures as primary option; move to automated rollback with human review after rollback completes.
Add: Console UI element for 'active fallback policy' per API key and per-route toggles (initial MVP with view-only before full edit controls).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Deterministic fallback behaves identically in simulation and production: internal canary runs show 100% of triggered fallbacks route to the configured model variant for 30 simulated breach events.
AC-2: Preflight validation prevents at least 95% of unsafe rollouts in staged test matrix (capacity mismatch, incompatible quantization kernels, KV health failcases).
AC-3: Canary failure-injection is integrated into CI and causes a deploy halt on any critical error; test matrix is documented and repeatable by Eng within 2 hours.
AC-4: Console dashboard surfaces fallback counts and cost deltas within 60s of occurrence and links to runbook; test by injecting synthetic events into observability pipelines.

AC-5: Automated rollback triggers when 1-minute P99 latency exceeds SLO by 30% for 3 consecutive minutes or when fallback fraction >15% sustained for 5 minutes; rollback completes and verifies pre-rollback state within 10 minutes in 90% of test runs.
AC-6: SDKs receive and expose the degraded-response typed signal for Go/TS/Python SDKs; unit tests demonstrate application-level handling of degraded responses.
AC-7: Security review completed and KMS/HSM interaction surfaces no new approval blockers for rollback automation.
success_metrics: Decrease in incident recurrence related to KV-induced fallback loops by >=80% in next 6 months.
Reduce mean incident detection-to-rollback time from current baseline (approx 18m) to <=10m for relevant classes.
Lower unexpected model routing variance during peak from current measured 4% to <1%.
95% of deploys must pass canary failure-injection in CI before reaching production.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement deterministic fallback logic behind a feature flag; enable on 5% of traffic with CI failure-injection running on canaries. Target: 2 sprints.
Phase 2 (preflight): Ship deployment preflight checks integrated into release pipeline; require green preflight for all model/runtime rollouts. Target: 1 sprint after Phase 1.
Phase 3 (console & SDK): Surface read-only fallback state in Console and add SDK degraded-response handling. Target: 2 sprints.
Phase 4 (automation & rollout): Activate automated rollback triggers and fully remove feature flag after 4 weeks stable canary data. Target: controlled ramp over 3 weeks.
Communication: announce to customers by email and changelog, with early notice for enterprise tenants that have custom Dedicated/private policies.
open_questions: Q1: Exact numeric thresholds for 'fallback fraction' and 'SLO breach'—should these be per-route or global by default? (Proposed: per-route with global defaults).
Q2: Which team owns the failure-injection matrix maintenance long-term? (Proposed: Reliability/Applied ML partnership).
Q3: What is the acceptable customer-facing degraded-response latency spike (ms budget) before marking as failed rollback?
Q4: Do Dedicated/private customers require opt-in for automated rollback?
decisions: Decision 1: Use deterministic, per-customer model variant mapping for fallbacks rather than random or best-effort selection.
Decision 2: Preflight checks will run in the control plane with read-only checks against customer VPC endpoints where allowed; results surface to Console.
Decision 3: Automated rollback is on by default for hosted accounts; Dedicated/private will default to notify-only and allow opt-in for automation.
